Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 14, verse 5:

The "days of Allah" have been explained as His blessings, and they have also been explained as His punishments upon the people of disbelief and sin. The first is the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Mujāhid, and the second is the explanation of Muqātil.

The correct view is that His days encompass both types: they are His battles which He inflicted upon His enemies, and His blessings which He bestowed upon His allies. These great blessings and punishments, which are recounted, are called "days" because they are the time frame for them. The Arabs say: "So-and-so is knowledgeable about the days of the Arabs and the days of the people," meaning, about the events that took place in those days. Knowledge of these days necessitates for the servant the insight to discern lessons, and in proportion to his knowledge of them will be his lesson-taking and his greatness. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Certainly there was in their stories a lesson for those of understanding﴾ [Yūsuf: 111].

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person﴾

He named Himself "Grateful" (shākir) and "Most Grateful" (shakūr), and He named the grateful by these two names. So He gave them a share of His attribute and named them by His name. Enough of this as evidence of His love for the grateful and of His favour toward them.

His returning to the grateful as "appreciated" (mashkūr): as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, this has been for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [al-Insān: 22].

The pleasure of the Lord with His servant for it: as in His saying: ﴿And if you are grateful, He is pleased with it for you﴾ [al-Zumar: 7]. And the scarcity of its people among the worlds indicates that they are His elite. As in His saying: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ [Saba': 13].

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he stood (in prayer) until his feet swelled. It was said to him: "You do this, while Allah has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what followed?" He said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?"

(Section: On how patience is half of faith)

Faith is of two halves: half patience and half gratitude. Several of the early scholars said: patience is half of faith.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Faith is of two halves: half patience and half gratitude."

For this reason Allah, glory be to Him, combined patience and gratitude in His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person﴾ in Sūrat Ibrāhīm, in Sūrat Ḥā Mīm ʿAsaq, in Sūrat Saba', and in Sūrat Luqmān.

Several considerations have been mentioned for this division into halves.

The first: faith is a name for the whole of speech, action and intention, and these return to two sides, doing and abstaining. Doing is acting in obedience to Allah, which is the reality of gratitude, and abstaining is patience in refraining from disobedience. The religion as a whole lies in these two things: doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden.

The second consideration: faith is built on two pillars, certainty and patience, which are the two pillars mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾.

Through certainty one knows the reality of the commands, the prohibitions, the reward and the punishment; through patience one carries out what one is commanded and restrains oneself from what one is forbidden. Affirmation that the commands and prohibitions are from Allah, and of the reward and punishment, is attained only through certainty; and one cannot persist in doing what is commanded and restraining oneself from what is forbidden except through patience. Thus patience becomes half of faith, and the second half is gratitude, by doing what one is commanded and by abandoning what one is forbidden.

(Another section)

Patience is half of faith, for it is a composite reality made of patience and gratitude, as some of the early scholars said: faith is of two halves: a half that is patience and a half that is gratitude. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 5]. Patience within faith is in the position of the head relative to the body, and it is of three kinds: patience upon the obligations of Allah, so that one does not neglect them; patience away from His prohibitions, so that one does not commit them; and patience upon His decrees and predestinations, so that one does not resent them. Whoever perfects these three levels perfects patience, and the enjoyment and bliss of this world and the Hereafter and their delights. Success and victory in both are not reached by anyone except over the bridge of patience, just as no one reaches Paradise except over the Ṣirāṭ. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The best life we have ever attained was through patience."

When you reflect upon the levels of perfection acquired in the world, you find them all contingent upon patience; and when you reflect upon the deficiency for which its possessor is blamed, and which falls within his power, you find it all stems from the lack of patience. Courage, chastity, generosity and selflessness are all a moment of patience.

> Patience is a talisman over the treasure of high station; whoever unlocks this talisman wins its treasure.

Most ailments of the body and heart arise only from lack of patience. The health of hearts, bodies and souls has not been preserved by anything like patience. It is the greatest criterion and the supreme antidote. Even if there were nothing in it but the companionship of Allah with its people, for Allah is with the patient and His love for them, for Allah loves the patient; and His help for its people, for help comes with patience, and it is good for its people: ﴿And if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient﴾ [al-Naḥl: 126]; and it is the cause of success: ﴿O you who have believed, be patient, outlast, remain stationed, and fear Allah that you may be successful﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 200].

(Section)

Consider what came about through the flood and the drowning of Pharaoh's people, for the nations, of guidance and faith, which overwhelmed the corruption of those who perished in it, until it dissolved in comparison with its benefit and wisdom. How many wisdoms belong to God in His signs, by which He tested His enemies and honored His allies in them, and how many signs, proofs, insights and reminders does He have in them. For this reason, glorified is He, He commanded His Messenger to remind his community with them, and God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], "Bring your people out of darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of God. Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful person." (5) And [mention] when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favor of God upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who subjected you to the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord."(6)﴾

So he reminded them of His days and His bounty, and of their deliverance from their enemy and his destruction while they were watching. Thereby there resulted from that remembrance, gratitude, love, glorification and reverence of Him, such that the corruption of the killing and slaughtering of the sons dissolved in it and vanished. For they went on to bliss and were freed from the corruption of servitude to Pharaoh when they grew up, whom he had subjected to the worst torment. The pain which the parents tasted at the slaughter was far lighter than the pains which they had swallowed through the enslavement of Pharaoh and his people to them. Thus the fathers and the sons both gained from that. God, glorified is He, also willed that His servants see what is among His greatest signs: that this infant, whom Pharaoh slaughtered the children of, as God willed, in seeking him, be raised in Pharaoh's household, in his house and upon his bed. How much wisdom, benefit, mercy, guidance and insight is contained within this verse, and it depends upon its necessary conditions and causes, and would not have existed without them, for that is impossible. Thus the benefit and wisdom of that sign overwhelmed the corruption of the slaughter of the sons and made it as if it had never been.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 14, verse 7:

Gratitude always brings increase with it, because of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]﴾.

So whenever you do not see your state as one of increase, then turn to gratitude.

In a divine report (athar ilahi), Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "The people of My remembrance are the people of My sitting (with Me), the people of My gratitude are the people of My increase, the people of My obedience are the people of My honor, and the people of My disobedience: I do not despair them of My mercy. If they repent, then I am their beloved, and if they do not repent, then I am their physician. I test them with calamities in order to purify them from faults."

It is said: Whoever conceals a blessing has denied it, and whoever makes it apparent and spreads it has thanked for it.

This is derived from his saying (ﷺ): "Indeed, when Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."

On this matter it has been said:

"Among the calamities is that my gratitude is silent about what you have done, while your goodness speaks;

And I see the favor from you, then I conceal it; indeed, then I would be a thief of the generosity of the noble."

(Section)

Blessings are three:

A blessing already attained, of which the servant is aware; a blessing awaited, which he hopes for; and a blessing he is in but does not perceive..

So when Allah wills to complete His blessing upon His servant, He makes him aware of his present blessing and gives him from His gratitude a fetter with which to bind it, so that it does not flee, for it flees through disobedience and is bound through gratitude.

He enables him to do a deed that draws the awaited blessing, and shows him the paths that block it and cut off its way, and enables him to avoid them.

Then behold, it has come to him in the most complete forms, and He makes him aware of the blessings he is in, so that he no longer perceives them.

It is related that a Bedouin entered upon al-Rashid and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, may Allah keep you steadfast in the blessings you are in by continuing to thank for them, fulfill for you the blessings you hope for through good opinion of Him and perpetual obedience to Him, and make you aware of the blessings you are in while not knowing them, so that you may thank for them."

This pleased him, and he said: "How excellent is his division."

(Admonition)

Ibn al-Mubarak said: I heard Ali ibn Salih say, concerning His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾:

He said: that is, [increase] from My obedience.

The verified view is that the increase is of blessings, and His obedience is for the sake of His blessings.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned that Muharib ibn Dithar used to stand in the night and sometimes raise his voice: "I am the little one whom You raised, so to You be praise; I am the weak one whom You strengthened, so to You be praise; I am the poor one whom You made rich, so to You be praise; I am the destitute one whom You supported, so to You be praise; I am the unmarried one whom You married, so to You be praise; I am the hungry one whom You fed, so to You be praise; I am the naked one whom You clothed, so to You be praise; I am the traveler whom You accompanied, so to You be praise; I am the absent one whom You returned, so to You be praise; I am the one on foot whom You carried, so to You be praise; I am the sick one whom You healed, so to You be praise; I am the petitioner whom You gave, so to You be praise; I am the supplicant whom You answered, so to You be praise. Our Lord, and to You be praise, abundant praise."

(Benefit)

Know that the blessings of Allah, mighty and majestic, have not been drawn down, nor has calamity been warded off, by anything like the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He.

So remembrance attracts blessings and repels calamities.

He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed﴾. In the other reading it is ﴿Indeed, Allah repels﴾. His repelling and defending on their behalf is in proportion to the strength and perfection of their faith.

The source and strength of faith is through the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He. Whoever is more complete in faith and more abundant in remembrance, Allah's repelling and defense for him is greater; and whoever is deficient, his [share] is diminished, remembrance for remembrance and forgetfulness for forgetfulness.

He, glorified and exalted, also said: ﴿And [recall] when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾. Remembrance is the head of gratitude, as has preceded, and gratitude attracts blessings and necessitates increase.

Some of the early pious predecessors, may Allah have mercy on them, said: How ugly is heedlessness of the remembrance of One who never forgets your remembrance.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 14, verse 10:

The messengers said to their peoples: ﴿Is there doubt about God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?﴾

Creation is innately disposed (mafṭūr, from fiṭra, the innate natural disposition) to know Him and to affirm His oneness. If people were left with this fiṭra, they would grow up knowing Him and worshipping Him alone. This fiṭra is a natural matter upon which they were created, and there is no alteration to the creation of God. People continued upon this fiṭra for many centuries. Then there arose something that caused its corruption and its departure from soundness and uprightness, like what afflicts a healthy body and a sound nature, which leads them away from health into deviation. So He sent His messengers to return people to their original fiṭra upon which they were created. Thus people divided into three categories with respect to the messengers.

Among them were those who responded to them completely and submitted to them entirely. Their fiṭra returned to what it had been, along with the perfection and completeness it gained in the two faculties of beneficial knowledge ('ilm nāfi') and righteous action ('amal ṣāliḥ). Thus their fiṭra increased in perfection upon its own perfection. These people do not need, in the Hereafter, to be refined and disciplined, nor to be purified by a fire that melts away their evil residues and cleanses them from filth and dirt, for their submission to the messengers removed all of that.

Another category responded to them partially, not wholly. Remnants of the grime and filth that contradict the truth for which they were created remained upon them. The All-Knowing, All-Wise therefore prepared for them remedies through trial and testing, in accordance with the afflictions that had taken hold of them. If these remedies suffice to free them in this world, well and good; otherwise, they are freed in the barzakh (intermediate realm). If that suffices, well and good; otherwise, the events of the Day of Resurrection and its terrors will cleanse them of that remaining residue. If even that does not suffice, then there must be treatment with the greatest remedy, and the last of the medicine is cauterization. They then enter the furnace of refinement and purification until, when they have been refined and the remedy no longer benefits them, they are brought out from the hospital of the sick to the abode of the healthy. This is indicated by the continuous (mutawātir) Sunnah from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he stated it explicitly in his saying:

"Until, when they have been refined and cleansed, permission is given to them to enter Paradise."

Likewise, the words of the Exalted: ﴿You are pure, so enter it, abiding therein forever.﴾ He did not permit them to enter it except after their purity, for it is the abode of the pure, and nothing of impurity whatsoever exists in it. For this reason, these people remain in the Fire for a period proportionate to their need for purification and the removal of impurity.

The third category are people who did not respond to the messengers nor submitted to them, but persisted in departing from the fiṭra and did not return to it. Their corruption became firmly established in them to the utmost degree, and no hope of their reform remains. The coming of this world, the calamities of death and what follows it, and the terrors of the Resurrection do not suffice to remove their filth and dirt. It is not befitting the wisdom of the All-Knowing, All-Wise that He should place them as neighbours to the pure in their abode, and they were not created for annihilation. These are the people of the abode of trial and testing, and they remain in it for as long as the stain of disbelief and polytheism remains with them. The Fire was kindled only upon them by their own evil deeds; their punishment is by the very essence of their evil actions, which take for them forms of punishment suited to and resembling them. The punishment remains upon them as long as the realities of those deeds and what springs from them remain. So long as the causes of punishment persist, the punishment persists.

(Section)

Consider the state of the whole world, its upper and lower parts, with all its components: you will find it bearing witness to the affirmation of its Maker, Originator and Sovereign. Denying its Maker and rejecting Him in intellects and natural dispositions is like denying and rejecting knowledge; there is no difference between them. Indeed, the indication of the Creator upon the created, of the Doer upon the deed, and of the Maker upon the condition of the made, is, to pure, luminous, lofty intellects and sound natural dispositions, clearer than the reverse.

The knowers, the masters of insight, reason from God to His acts and works, just as people reason from His works and acts to Him. There is no doubt that both are sound paths, each of them true, and the Qur'an comprises both.

As for reasoning from the making (ṣan'a), it is abundant. As for reasoning from the Maker Himself, it has a particular rank, and this is what the messengers pointed to with their words to their peoples: ﴿Is there doubt about God?﴾ [Ibrahim: 10], meaning: Is God doubted, such that proof of His existence must be sought? What proof is more sound and more manifest than this object of proof? How, then, can the more manifest be proved by the less manifest? Then they drew attention to the proof with their words ﴿the Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyya, may God sanctify his spirit, say: "How is proof sought for Him who is Himself the proof of everything?" He frequently recited this verse of poetry:

"Nothing can be established in minds
when daylight needs a proof."

It is well known that the existence of the Lord, exalted is He, is clearer to intellects and natural dispositions than the existence of daytime. Whoever does not perceive this in his intellect and his natural disposition, let him suspect both of them.

The servant's affliction is either from lacking guidance or from lacking reliance (tawakkul). So whoever combines reliance with guidance has combined all of faith.

Yes, reliance on God regarding provision that is known and guaranteed, and being occupied with it instead of with reliance in supporting the truth and the religion, is among the weakest stations of the elite. As for relying on Him to obtain what He loves and is pleased with, both in oneself and in creation, this is the reliance of the Messengers and Prophets, peace be upon them.

(Section)

The messengers said to their people: ﴿And why should we not rely upon God, when He has guided us to our paths?﴾ They marvelled at their abandoning reliance on God when He is the one who guided them, and they affirmed that this could never be.

This is evidence that guidance and reliance are mutually entailed. The one who encounters the truth, through his knowledge of the truth and his certainty that God is the ally of the truth and its supporter, is compelled to rely on Him and finds no alternative to it. For reliance (tawakkul) comprises two foundations: the knowledge of the heart and its action.

As for its knowledge: certainty in the sufficiency of one's Trustee, the perfection of His management of what He has entrusted to Him, and that no one else can stand in His place in that. As for its action: the heart's repose in its Trustee, its tranquillity in Him, and its entrusting and surrendering its affair to Him, and that no one else can stand in His place in that. And its contentment with His disposal on its behalf is greater than its contentment with its own disposal for itself. By these two foundations reliance is realized, and they are its essence, although reliance has entered into the actions of the heart as one of its deeds, as Imam Ahmad said: "Reliance is an action of the heart," but it necessarily involves knowledge, which is either a condition for it or a part of its essence.

The point is that whenever the heart is upon the truth, it is more conducive to its tranquillity, its confidence that God is its ally and supporter, and its repose in Him. How could it fail to rely on its Lord? Whenever it is upon falsehood, in knowledge and action or in one of them, it will not be tranquil or confident in its Lord, for it has no guarantee from Him and no covenant with Him. God, glorified is He, does not take falsehood as an ally and does not support it, and it is not attributed to Him in any way; it is wholly cut off from relation to Him. For He, glorified is He, is the Truth, His word is true, His religion is true, His promise is true, His meeting is true, and all His acts are true.

There is nothing false in His actions; rather His actions, glorified is He, are free of falsehood, just as His words, glorified is He, are likewise. Since falsehood has no connection to Him, glorified is He, but is utterly severed from Him, so is its adherent. Whoever has no connection to the Mighty God, and is cut off from his Lord, God is not his ally, nor his supporter, nor his trustee.

So reflect upon this great secret in the conjunction of reliance and sufficiency with truth and guidance, and the linkage of each to the other. Were there no benefit in this treatise except this hidden benefit, it would be a truth worthy of being deposited in the treasury of the heart, given the great need for it. And God is the one sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

Thus it becomes clear that reliance (tawakkul) is the foundation of all the stations of faith (iman) and excellence (ihsan), and of all the works of Islam, and that its position relative to them is that of the body to the head: just as the head cannot stand except upon the body, so faith, its stations, and its works cannot stand except upon the leg of reliance. And God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 14, verse 16:

His saying: ﴿Before him is Hell﴾ (note: the Arabic is "min warā'ihi jahannamu," which the translation renders as "Before him is Hell" only where the commentary explains it; see below). The meaning is that he will meet Hell after his death, so it is "from after him," i.e., after his departure from this world. Since "warā'" (behind/after) follows his life, it is "behind him," because warā' is like ba'd (after). Just as ba'd cannot be qabl (before), warā' cannot be amām (in front). If you said "Hell is after the death of the disbeliever," there would be no sense of "before" in it in any way.

So warā' here is a matter of time, not place, so reflect on it, may Allah have mercy on you. It is behind the time of his life and after it, and it is in front of him and facing him. Its being "behind" and "in front" is from two different perspectives. The confusion arose because the "afterness" of time occurs only in what is ahead of you, like your saying "the day after tomorrow," while the "behindness" of place occurs in what is left behind your back. So "min warā'ihi jahannamu" refers to the behindness of time, not place, and it occurs only in the future that is in front of you. Since the sense of "in front" is necessarily attached to it, whoever thought it was shared (between both senses) was mistaken; there is no sharing in it. Likewise His saying: ﴿And behind him is a severe punishment﴾, and likewise: ﴿Before him is Hell﴾.

Glorified is He. He likened the deeds of the disbelievers, in their futility and their failure to benefit anyone, to ashes over which a violent wind has blown on a stormy day. He, glorified, likened their deeds, in their being nullified and gone as mere vanity, to scattered dust (*al-habaʾ al-manthur*), because they are not founded on faith and excellence, because they are for other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and because they are not in accordance with His command. They are like ashes that a fierce wind has scattered, so that their owner has none of it at the time of his greatest need for it. Therefore He said: ﴿They have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾ [Ibrahim: 18]. On the Day of Resurrection they will have no power over anything of the deeds they earned, so they will find no trace of them in reward and no beneficial gain. Allah does not accept any deed except what is sincerely for His sake and conforms to His law. Deeds are of four kinds: one is accepted and three are rejected. The accepted one is that which is sincere and correct. Sincerity means that it is for Allah and not for other than Him. Correctness means that it is of what Allah has prescribed through His Messenger (ﷺ). The three rejected kinds are those that contravene this.

In likening them to ashes there is a wondrous secret, namely the resemblance between their deeds and ashes: both are what fire has burned and destroyed down to their origin. Thus deeds done for other than Allah and not for His sake became fuel for the Fire, by which the Fire is kindled against their doers. Allah, glorified, produces for them from their vain deeds a fire and a punishment, just as He produces for the people of deeds that conform to His command and prohibition, which are sincerely for His sake, bliss and comfort. The Fire has affected the deeds of those people until it has made them ashes. They, their deeds, and what they worshipped besides Allah are the fuel of the Fire.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 14, verse 22:

The authority (al-sultan) denied in this place is the proof and the evidence, i.e., I had no proof or evidence over you with which I could argue against you, as Ibn 'Abbas said: "I had no proof with which to argue against you."

That is: I showed you no proof, except that I called you and you responded to me, accepted my words, and followed me without any evidence or proof.

As for the authority (sultan) that he affirmed in His words: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾ [al-Nahl: 100],

it is his domination over them through seduction and misguidance, and his power over them, such that he incites them toward disbelief and polytheism and drives them to it, and does not leave them to abandon it, as the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not seen that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?﴾ [Maryam: 83].

Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir (Commentary) on Surah 14, verses 24–25:

Allah, glorified and exalted, compared the good word (al-kalimah al-tayyibah) to the good tree (al-shajarah al-tayyibah), because the good word produces righteous deeds, just as the good tree produces beneficial fruit.

This is evident according to the view of the majority of the exegetes (mufassirun), who say: "The good word is the testimony that there is no god but Allah." For it produces all righteous deeds, both outward and inward, so every deed that is righteous and pleasing to Allah is a fruit of this word.

In the tafsir of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, he said: "The good word is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, like a good tree, which is the believer. Its root is firmly established: the saying 'there is no god but Allah' in the heart of the believer, and its branch is in the sky: by it the believer's deed is raised to the sky."

Al-Rabi ibn Anas said: "The good word is an example of faith. Faith is the good tree, and its firmly established root, which does not disappear, is sincerity (al-ikhlas) in it, and its branch in the sky is the fear of Allah."

The comparison according to this view is more correct, clearer and more excellent, for He, glorified is He, compared the tree of monotheism (tawhid) in the heart to the good tree, whose root is firmly established and whose branches are lofty in the sky, which never stops yielding its fruit in every season. When you reflect on this comparison, you will see that it corresponds to the tree of tawhid, firmly rooted in the heart, whose branches of righteous deeds ascend to the sky. This tree never ceases to produce righteous deeds at all times, in accordance with its steadfastness in the heart, the heart's love for it, its sincerity in it, its knowledge of its reality, its fulfilment of its rights, and its observance of its due observance. Whoever has this word firmly planted in his heart with its true reality, and his heart is characterized by it and colored by it with the color of Allah, than which there is no better color, and knows the reality of divinity (al-ilahiyyah) which his heart affirms for Allah, which his tongue testifies to and his limbs confirm, and negates that reality and its implications from everything other than Allah, and his heart agrees with his tongue in this negation and affirmation, and his limbs submit to the One to whom he testified unity, obediently, following the paths of his Lord, humbly, not deviating from them nor seeking any other in their place, just as the heart does not seek any other object of worship in place of the true God.

There is no doubt that this word, from this heart, upon this tongue, continues to yield its fruit of righteous deeds ascending to Allah at all times. This good word is what raised this righteous deed to the Lord, the Exalted, and this good word produces many good words, accompanied by a righteous deed, so the righteous deed raises the good word, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. So He, glorified is He, informed that the righteous deed raises the good word, and informed that the good word produces for its speaker a righteous deed at all times.

[The effect of the word of tawhid]

The point is that the word of tawhid, when the believer testifies to it, knowing its meaning and reality, in negation and affirmation, characterized by its requirement, with his heart, tongue and limbs standing by his testimony, this good word is what raises this deed from this witness. Its root is firmly established in his heart, its branches connected to the sky, and it continually brings forth its fruit.

Among the early generation (al-salaf) were those who said: the good tree is the palm tree, and the authentic hadith of Ibn Umar indicates this. Others said: it is the believer himself, as Muhammad ibn Sa'd said: my father related to me, my paternal uncle related to me, my father related to me from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾ [Ibrahim: 24], meaning by the good tree the believer, and by the firmly established root in the earth and the branch in the sky, the believer works on the earth and speaks, and his deed and speech reach the sky while he is on the earth.

Atiyyah al-Awfi said, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾ [Ibrahim: 24]: that is the example of the believer, from whom there continually comes forth good speech and righteous deeds that ascend to Allah.

Al-Rabi ibn Anas said, regarding: ﴿Its root is firmly established and its branch is in the sky﴾ [Ibrahim: 24]: that is the believer, whose example Allah struck in sincerity to Allah alone and worship of Him alone, without partner. Its root is firmly established: the root of his deed is firmly established on the earth, and its branch is in the sky. He said: his remembrance is in the sky. There is no contradiction between the two sayings. The example refers to the believer, and the palm tree is likened to him, and he is likened to it. If the palm tree is a good tree, then the believer likened to it is more worthy of being so. And whoever among the early generation said it is a tree in Paradise, then the palm tree is among the noblest trees of Paradise.

[Some secrets of likening the believer to a tree]

In this example are secrets, knowledge and insights fitting to it, which the wisdom and knowledge of the One who spoke it require.

Among them: a tree must have roots, a trunk, branches, leaves and fruit. Likewise the tree of faith and Islam, so that the thing compared matches the thing it is compared to. Its roots are knowledge, recognition and certainty; its trunk is sincerity; its branches are deeds; and its fruit is what righteous deeds necessitate of praiseworthy effects, commendable qualities, pure morals, good bearing, and approved guidance and humility. By these matters, the planting of this tree in the heart and its firmness in it are inferred. When knowledge is sound, corresponding to what is known which Allah revealed in His Book, and belief corresponds to what He informed about Himself and what His messengers informed about Him, and sincerity stands in the heart, and deeds conform to the command, and guidance, humility and bearing resemble these roots and are in harmony with them, it is known that the tree of faith in the heart has a firm root and its branch is in the sky. And if the matter is the reverse, it is known that what stands in the heart is the wicked tree which has been uprooted from above the earth, having no stability.

Among them: a tree cannot remain alive except by a substance that waters it and makes it grow. If watering is cut off from it, it is about to dry up. Likewise the tree of Islam in the heart: if its owner does not tend to watering it at all times with beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, returning from forgetfulness to reflection and from reflection to remembrance, it is about to dry up. In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, he said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «Faith wears out in the heart just as clothing wears out, so renew your faith.» In sum, if the owner does not tend to a planting, it is about to perish. From here you learn the great need of the servants for what Allah has commanded of acts of worship over the succession of times, the greatness of His mercy, the completeness of His grace and His kindness to His servants, in that He assigned them to these, and made them a means of watering the plantings of tawhid which He planted in their hearts.

Among them: Allah, glorified is He, has established the custom that planting and beneficial crops inevitably become mixed with weeds and foreign growth not of their kind. If the owner tends to it, cleans it and uproots them, the planting and crop are perfected, stand straight, complete their growth, and are fuller in fruit, better and purer. If he leaves them, the weeds are about to overcome the planting and crop and take control, or weaken the root and make the fruit blameworthy and deficient, according to their abundance or scarcity. Whoever lacks insight into this and knowledge of it will miss a great profit without realizing it. The believer's effort is always in two things: watering this tree and clearing what surrounds it. By watering it, it remains and endures; by clearing what surrounds it, it becomes complete and perfect. And Allah is the One sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

This is some of what this great and glorious example contains of secrets and wisdoms. Perhaps it is but a drop from an ocean, according to our limited minds, our erring hearts, our deficient knowledge, and our deeds which require repentance and seeking forgiveness. Otherwise, if our hearts were purified, our minds clarified, our souls purified, our deeds sincere, and they were free to receive from Allah and His Messenger, we would witness in the meanings of the speech of Allah, its secrets and wisdoms, what knowledge dissolves before and the knowledge of creation vanishes. By this you know the worth of the knowledge and insights of the Companions, and that the difference between their knowledge and the knowledge of those after them is like the difference between them in virtue. And Allah knows best where He places His bounty and whom He specially favors with His mercy.

(Section)

The year is a tree, the months are its branches, the days are its boughs, the hours are its leaves, and the breaths are its fruit. Whoever's breaths are in obedience, the fruit of his tree is good; whoever's are in disobedience, his fruit is colocynth. The harvest is only on the Day of Return, and at the harvest the sweet fruit is distinguished from the bitter. Sincerity and tawhid are a tree in the heart: its branches are deeds, and its fruit is the good life in this world and everlasting bliss in the Hereafter. Just as the fruits of Paradise are neither cut off nor forbidden, so too the fruit of tawhid and sincerity in this world. The shirk, lying and showing-off are a tree in the heart whose fruit in this world is fear, worry, grief, constriction of the chest and darkness of the heart, and whose fruit in the Hereafter is the zaqqum tree and lasting punishment. Allah mentioned these two trees in Surah Ibrahim.

(Admonition)

The tree of sincerity has a firm root; no gusts of wind harm it. ﴿Where are My partners that you used to claim?﴾

As for the tree of the gourd, it is uprooted at the breath of one who worshipped something, so let him follow it.

The showing-off of the show-offs turns the mosque of harm into a dunghill and a ruin; never stand in it. The sincerity of the sincere raises the rank above the impurity.

How many a disheveled, dusty-faced one, whose heart you show off to, with a hand from which you turned away; he turns you away from Him to another, so you have obtained neither the reward of the sincere nor reached what you intended by showing off; the reward and praise are lost, neither this nor that.

Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir (Commentary) on Surah 14, verses 24–25:

Allah, glorified and exalted, compared the good word (al-kalimah al-tayyibah) to the good tree (al-shajarah al-tayyibah), because the good word produces righteous deeds, just as the good tree produces beneficial fruit.

This is evident according to the view of the majority of the exegetes (mufassirun), who say: "The good word is the testimony that there is no god but Allah." For it produces all righteous deeds, both outward and inward, so every deed that is righteous and pleasing to Allah is a fruit of this word.

In the tafsir of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, he said: "The good word is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, like a good tree, which is the believer. Its root is firmly established: the saying 'there is no god but Allah' in the heart of the believer, and its branch is in the sky: by it the believer's deed is raised to the sky."

Al-Rabi ibn Anas said: "The good word is an example of faith. Faith is the good tree, and its firmly established root, which does not disappear, is sincerity (al-ikhlas) in it, and its branch in the sky is the fear of Allah."

The comparison according to this view is more correct, clearer and more excellent, for He, glorified is He, compared the tree of monotheism (tawhid) in the heart to the good tree, whose root is firmly established and whose branches are lofty in the sky, which never stops yielding its fruit in every season. When you reflect on this comparison, you will see that it corresponds to the tree of tawhid, firmly rooted in the heart, whose branches of righteous deeds ascend to the sky. This tree never ceases to produce righteous deeds at all times, in accordance with its steadfastness in the heart, the heart's love for it, its sincerity in it, its knowledge of its reality, its fulfilment of its rights, and its observance of its due observance. Whoever has this word firmly planted in his heart with its true reality, and his heart is characterized by it and colored by it with the color of Allah, than which there is no better color, and knows the reality of divinity (al-ilahiyyah) which his heart affirms for Allah, which his tongue testifies to and his limbs confirm, and negates that reality and its implications from everything other than Allah, and his heart agrees with his tongue in this negation and affirmation, and his limbs submit to the One to whom he testified unity, obediently, following the paths of his Lord, humbly, not deviating from them nor seeking any other in their place, just as the heart does not seek any other object of worship in place of the true God.

There is no doubt that this word, from this heart, upon this tongue, continues to yield its fruit of righteous deeds ascending to Allah at all times. This good word is what raised this righteous deed to the Lord, the Exalted, and this good word produces many good words, accompanied by a righteous deed, so the righteous deed raises the good word, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. So He, glorified is He, informed that the righteous deed raises the good word, and informed that the good word produces for its speaker a righteous deed at all times.

[The effect of the word of tawhid]

The point is that the word of tawhid, when the believer testifies to it, knowing its meaning and reality, in negation and affirmation, characterized by its requirement, with his heart, tongue and limbs standing by his testimony, this good word is what raises this deed from this witness. Its root is firmly established in his heart, its branches connected to the sky, and it continually brings forth its fruit.

Among the early generation (al-salaf) were those who said: the good tree is the palm tree, and the authentic hadith of Ibn Umar indicates this. Others said: it is the believer himself, as Muhammad ibn Sa'd said: my father related to me, my paternal uncle related to me, my father related to me from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree﴾ [Ibrahim: 24], meaning by the good tree the believer, and by the firmly established root in the earth and the branch in the sky, the believer works on the earth and speaks, and his deed and speech reach the sky while he is on the earth.

[Section: The Parable of the Disbeliever]

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the parable of the evil word, likening it to the evil tree which has been uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. It has no firmly rooted root, no high branch, and no pure fruit. Thus it has no shade, no fruit to pick, and no upright trunk. It has no root fixed in the earth, so there is no abundant water beneath it and no beauty above it, and there is no harvest from it. It does not rise up; rather, it is brought low.

When the discerning person reflects upon most of the speech of these creatures, in their discourse and their earnings, he will find that it is like this. Thus, the loss lies in standing with it and being occupied with it instead of with the best and most beneficial speech.

Al-Dahhak said: Allah struck a parable for the disbeliever with a tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. He says: it has no root and no branch, it has no fruit, and there is no benefit in it. Likewise the disbeliever does not do good nor say it, and Allah does not place in him any blessing or benefit.

Ibn Abbas said: "And the parable of an evil word" (Ibrahim: 26), which is shirk, "like an evil tree" (Ibrahim: 26), meaning the disbeliever, "uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability" (Ibrahim: 26). He says: shirk has no root which the disbeliever can hold to, nor any proof, and Allah does not accept any deed along with shirk. So the deed of the polytheist is not accepted and does not ascend to Allah. It has no firm root in the earth nor a branch in the heaven. He says: it has no righteous deed in the heavens or on the earth.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The parable of the evil tree is the parable of the disbeliever. His saying and his deed have neither root nor branch, and his saying and his deed do not settle on the earth, nor do they ascend to the heaven.

Sa'id reported from Qatadah concerning this verse: A man met a man of knowledge and said to him, "What do you say about the evil word?" He said, "I know of no settlement for it on the earth, nor any ascent for it in the heaven, except that it clings to the neck of its owner until he is brought with it on the Day of Resurrection."

As for His saying, "uprooted" (Ibrahim: 26), it means it was torn out completely from the surface of the earth.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 14, verse 27 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, glorified is He, informed us of His grace and His justice regarding the two groups: the people of the good word and the people of the evil word. He informed us that He makes firm those who believe, by their faith, with the firm word, at the time they most need it in this world and the Hereafter, and that He leads astray the wrongdoers, who are the polytheists, from the firm word. So He misguided these by His justice because of their wrongdoing, and made the believers firm by His grace because of their faith.

Beneath His saying: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27] lies a great treasure. Whoever is granted success in reaching its source, excels in extracting it, acquiring it, and spending from it, has gained; and whoever is deprived of it has been deprived. This is because the servant is never independent of Allah's making him firm even for the blink of an eye. If He does not make him firm, the heaven and earth of his faith would be displaced from their places. The Exalted said to the noblest of His creation before Him, His servant and Messenger: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined to them a little﴾ [al-Isra: 74]. And the Exalted said to the noblest of His creation: ﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so make firm those who believe"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]. And in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Bajali, he said: "while he was asking them and making them firm." And the Exalted said to His Messenger: ﴿And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that with which We make firm your heart﴾ [Hud: 120].

So all of creation is of two kinds: one granted success through being made firm, and one forsaken by being left unfirmed. The material of firmness, its root and origin, is the firm word and the doing of what the servant has been commanded. By these two, Allah makes His servant firm. So whoever is firmer in speech and better in deed is greater in being made firm. The Exalted said: ﴿And had they done what they were admonished with, it would have been better for them and stronger in firmness﴾ [al-Nisa: 66]. So the firmest of people in heart are the firmest of them in speech. The firm word is the true and sincere word, and it is the opposite of the false, lying word. Speech is of two kinds: firm, which has a reality, and false, which has no reality. The firmest speech is the word of tawhid and its necessities, and it is the greatest thing with which Allah makes His servant firm in this world and the Hereafter. For this reason you find the truthful to be the firmest and most courageous of people in heart, and the liar to be the most contemptible and most wicked of people, the most soiled and the least firm. The people of physiognomy know the truthfulness of the truthful from the steadiness of his heart at the time of speaking, and his courage and dignity, and they know the lying of the liar by the opposite of that; and this is hidden only from the one of weak insight.

Someone was asked about a speech he had heard from a speaker, and he said: "By Allah, I did not understand anything from it, except that I saw in his speech a force that is not the force of one who is false. A servant is granted no gift better than the gift of the firm word, and the people of the firm word find its fruit at the time they most need it, in their graves and on the day of their resurrection, as in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said that this verse was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave."

[Questioning in the grave and being made firm therein]

This has been explained in sound hadiths. Among them is what is in the Musnad from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadra, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) at a funeral, and he said: 'O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his companions have dispersed from him, an angel comes to him with a hammer in his hand and seats him and says: What do you say about this man? If he was a believer, he says: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. So it is said to him: You have spoken the truth. Then a door to the Fire is opened for him and it is said to him: This is your abode had you disbelieved in your Lord; but since you believed, Allah has replaced it for you with this. Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he wishes to rise toward it, but it is said to him: Be still. Then his grave is widened for him. As for the disbeliever and the hypocrite, it is said to him: What do you say about this man? He says: I do not know. It is said to him: You did not know and you were not guided. Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: This is your abode had you believed in your Lord; but since you disbelieved, Allah has replaced it for you with this. Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, then the angel strikes him with the hammer a blow that is heard by all of Allah's creation except the two worlds of jinn and men.' Some of his companions said: 'O Messenger of Allah, none of us is there when an angel stands over his head with a hammer in his hand except that he is terrified at that moment.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim: 27]." In the Musnad there is something similar from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.

Al-Minhal ibn 'Amr related from Zadhan, from al-Bara', who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer and said: There comes to him a comer, meaning in his grave, and he says: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet? He says: My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad. He said: Then he [the comer] rebukes him and says: What is your Lord? What is your religion? And this is the last trial presented to the believer. That is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27]. He says: My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad. So it is said to him: You have spoken the truth." And this is a sound hadith.

Hammad ibn Salama said, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers﴾ [Ibrahim: 27]. He said: When it is said to him in the grave: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? He says: My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, who came to us with the clear proofs from Allah, so I believed in him and affirmed him. So it is said to him: You have spoken the truth. Upon this you lived, upon this you died, and upon this you will be resurrected."

Al-A'mash said, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, and from Zadhan, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer: He said: His soul returns into his body, and two angels of severe rebuke are sent to him. They seat him and rebuke him and say: Who is your Lord? He says: Allah. What is your religion? He says: Islam. They say to him: What is this man, or the Prophet, who was sent among you? He says: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. They say to him: And how do you know? He says: I recited the Book of Allah, so I believed in it and affirmed it. That is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27]."

Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih, and Imam Ahmad, and in his Sahih also, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, raising it: "Indeed the deceased hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away from him retreating. If he was a believer, the prayer will be at his head, the zakat at his right, the fasting at his left, and the doing of good deeds, of charity, kinship, kindness and goodness to people, at his feet. He is approached from his head, and the prayer says: There is no entrance from my side. He is approached from his right, and the zakat says: There is no entrance from my side. He is approached from his left, and the fasting says: There is no entrance from my side. He is approached from his feet, and the doing of good deeds, of charity, kinship, kindness and goodness to people says: There is no entrance from my side. Then it is said to him: Sit up. He sits up, and the sun has been depicted for him, drawing near to setting. He is told: Tell us about what we ask you. He says: Let me pray first. It is said: You will indeed do so; but tell us about what we ask. He says: What are you asking me about? It is said to him: Tell us about this man who was among you: what do you say about him, and what do you testify concerning him? He says: Muhammad (ﷺ)? It is said: Yes. He says: I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, and that he came with the clear proofs from Allah, so we affirmed him. It is said to him: Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, if Allah wills. Then his grave is widened for him seventy cubits, and it is illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: Look at what Allah has prepared for you in it. He grows in delight and joy. Then his soul is placed among the good breaths, which are green birds hanging from the trees of Paradise, and the body is returned to what it began from, the dust." That is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

This digression should not be considered lengthy by the mufti, the witness and the judge; indeed every Muslim has more need of it than of food, drink and breath. And success is from Allah.

[Section: Sins weaken the servant before his own self]

Among its punishments is that it betrays the servant at the time he most needs his own self. Every person needs to know what benefits him and what harms him in his livelihood and his return, and the most knowledgeable of people are those who know this in detail; the strongest and shrewdest of them are those who have power over their own selves and their wills, so they employ them in what benefits them and restrain them from what harms them.

People differ in their knowledge, aspirations and ranks in this: the most knowledgeable of them is one who knows the causes of happiness and misery, and the most rightly guided of them is one who prefers the former over the latter, just as the most foolish of them is one who reverses the matter.

Sins betray the servant when he most needs his self to acquire this knowledge and to prefer the lofty, exalted, lasting share over the lowly, base, cut-off share. Sins veil him from the perfection of this knowledge and from occupying himself with what is more fitting for him and more beneficial to him in both abodes.

When something disliked occurs and he needs to be freed from it, his heart, his self and his limbs betray him, and he is like a man who has a sword that has been covered with rust and is stuck in its sheath, so that it does not come out when its owner pulls it. Then an enemy confronts him who wants to kill him, so he places his hand on the hilt of his sword and strives to draw it out, but it does not come out with him; so the enemy overwhelms him and gains the upper hand over him.

Likewise the heart rusts through sins and becomes wounded by disease; when it needs to fight the enemy, it finds nothing of its strength with it. The servant only fights, struggles and advances with his heart, and the limbs follow the heart. If the king of the limbs does not have power by which to repel, what then is the assumption regarding them?

Likewise the self: it becomes corrupt through desires and sins and grows weak, I mean the at-peace self (al-nafs al-mutma'inna), though if the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammara) grows strong and becomes fierce, whenever this grows strong that weakens, and the ruling and disposing remains with the commanding self.

Perhaps his at-peace self dies a death from which no life is hoped for that would benefit him; rather his life becomes a life through which he perceives only pain.

The point is that when the servant falls into hardship, distress or affliction, his heart, tongue and limbs betray him in what is most beneficial to him. His heart is not drawn to trust in Allah, the Exalted, to turning to Him in repentance, to gathering upon Him, to humbling and abasing himself before Him, and to submission before Him; his tongue does not obey him in remembering Him; and if he remembers Him with his tongue, he does not join his heart and tongue together. The heart is then bound to the tongue in such a way that the remembrance has no effect, and the heart and tongue are not bound to the remembrance; rather, if he remembers or supplicates, he does so with a heart that is heedless, inattentive and negligent. Even if he wants his limbs to help him by an act of obedience that would repel harm from him, they do not comply with him and do not obey him.

All of this is the effect of sins and transgressions, like one who has an army that repels enemies from him, but he neglects his army, wastes them, weakens them, and cuts off news of them; then when the enemy assails him he demands of them that they exhaust their power in repelling for him without strength.

Moreover, there is a matter more frightening than that, more calamitous and more bitter: that his heart and tongue betray him at the time of dying and departing to Allah, the Exalted. Perhaps the pronouncing of the testimony becomes impossible for him, as people have witnessed in many of the dying who suffered that. It was said to one of them: "Say: there is no god but Allah." He said: "Ah, ah, I cannot say it."

It was said to another: "Say: there is no god but Allah." He said: "Shah-rukh, I have defeated you." Then he died.

It was said to another: "Say: there is no god but Allah." He said:

؎O many a sleeper who, one day, grew weary, asking: "Where is the road to the bathhouse of Minjab?"
Then he died.

It was said to another: "Say, 'There is no god but Allah.'" He began babbling with singing and saying: "Tatna tinintā," until he died.

It was said to another of them the same, and he said: "What use is what you say to me, when I have not left a sin without committing it?" Then he died without saying it.

It was said to another of them the same, and he said: "What avails me, and I do not know that I ever prayed a single prayer to Allah?" Then he died without saying it.

It was said to another of them the same, and he said: "He is a disbeliever in what you say." And he died.

It was said to another of them the same, and he said: "Every time I want to say it, my tongue holds back from it."

Someone who was present with some of the beggars at their death told me that they kept saying: "For Allah, a fils for Allah!" until he died.

Some merchants told me about a relative of his who was at the point of death while he was with him. They began prompting him: "There is no god but Allah," but he kept saying: "This piece is cheap, this buyer is good, this is such-and-such," until he died.

Glory be to Allah! How many lessons have people witnessed from this? What is hidden from them of the states of the dying is greater and still greater.

So if the servant, in a state of full mental presence, strength and complete perception, has been overcome by Satan, who makes him serve what he wills of the disobedience of Allah, and has made his heart heedless of the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, has rendered his tongue idle from remembering Him and his limbs idle from obeying Him, then what is to be expected of him when his powers collapse and his heart and breath are preoccupied with the pain of the death-agony? Satan will gather for him all his strength and resolve, and muster against him everything he is able to, so that he may attain his opportunity, for that is the last of the deed. The Satan of that time is at his strongest, and the person himself is at his weakest in that state. So who, then, will be safe in such a condition? At that point, ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah sends astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

How, then, can one be granted a good end (ḥusn al-khātimah, the good final outcome of one's life) when Allah the Glorified has left his heart heedless of His remembrance, he follows his desire, and his affair is ﴿neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]? Far away is the one whose heart is far from Allah the Exalted, heedless of Him, a worshipper of his desire, a captive of his appetites, whose tongue is dry of His remembrance and whose limbs are idle from obeying Him and busy with disobeying Him, from being granted a good end.

The fear of the final end (khawf al-khātimah) has indeed weighed heavily on the backs of the God-fearing, while the wrongdoing evildoers seem to have obtained a signed guarantee of safety. ﴿Or do you have oaths binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed you will have whatever you judge? Ask them which of them will stand surety for that﴾ [al-Qalam: 39–40].

As it has been said:

؎O you who feel secure from the evil of his deeds, has there come to you a decree of safety that you possess?
؎You have combined two things: security and the following of desire. This, and one of them, destroys a person.
؎The doers of good have walked the path of fears, and that is a path you do not walk.
؎You neglected sowing at the time of planting, out of foolishness, so how will you reach the harvest that people reap?
؎And the most astonishing thing about you is your renunciation of the abode of permanence, for a life you will surely leave behind.
؎So who is the fool then, by Allah: you, or the one who is cheated in a sale, a loss he will surely encounter?

(Section)

The Lord, blessed is His name and exalted is His majesty, and there is no god but Him, is truly the Bestower of blessings of every kind, which the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth cannot count. Their being brought into existence is a blessing from Him; making them living, speaking beings is a blessing from Him; giving them hearing, sight and intellect is a blessing from Him; providing them with sustenance in its various kinds and categories is a blessing from Him; making Himself known to them by His names, attributes and actions is a blessing from Him; causing His remembrance to be on their tongues and His love and knowledge to be in their hearts is a blessing from Him; preserving them after their creation is a blessing from Him; His managing their affairs, the minute and the great, is a blessing from Him; and guiding them to the means of their welfare and livelihood is a blessing from Him. Enumerating His blessings in detail is a path no one can take, and no human has the ability to do it.

It suffices that breath alone, which is among the least of His blessings that they scarcely reckon, amounts to twenty-four thousand breaths every day and night. Thus the servant has, in respect of breath alone, twenty-four thousand blessings from God every day and night, leaving aside what is other than that from the kinds of His blessings upon the servant. For each of these blessings there is a right of thanks that it requires and demands. If all of the servant's acts of obedience were distributed over these blessings, the share of each blessing would amount only to a very small part, bearing no proportion whatsoever to the measure of that blessing.

(Benefit)

Some preachers used to say in their sermon: "He fashioned the nose for you, erected it, completed it and perfected its completion. Then He arranged the eyeball for you, setting it within closed eyelids and suspended lashes. He moved you from stage to stage. He inclined toward you the hearts of your parents with tenderness and affection. His blessings upon you are in leaf, and His bounties surround you."

Some scholars used to say, regarding the Exalted's words ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾:

"Glory be to Him who did not make the attainment of knowledge of His blessings for anyone except the knowledge of falling short of comprehending them, just as He did not make the attainment of perception of Him for anyone more than the knowledge that one cannot perceive Him. So He made the knowledge of one's shortcoming in grasping His blessings a form of thanks, just as He thanked the knowledge of the knowers that they cannot perceive Him, and made it faith, knowing that the servants do not go beyond that."

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Mathna ibn al-Sabah informed us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:

"Whoever has two qualities, Allah records him as patient and thankful; and whoever lacks them, Allah does not record him as patient and thankful: whoever looks in matters of his religion to one who is above him and follows his example, and looks in matters of his worldly life to one who is below him [, Allah records him as patient and thankful]. Whoever praises Allah for what He has favored him with, Allah records him as patient and thankful. Whoever looks in matters of his religion to one who is below him, and looks in matters of his worldly life to one who is above him, and so regrets what has escaped him of it, Allah does not record him as patient and thankful."

(Section)

As for witnessing the blessing, it leaves no good deed of his that he sees at all, even if he performed the deeds of both jinn and humankind, for the blessings of Allah, glorified is He, exceed his deeds, and the least of His blessings consumes his deed. So the servant should not cease to look at what is God's right upon him.

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Wahb, who said: It reached me that the Prophet of Allah Musa (peace be upon him) passed by a man who was supplicating and humbling himself, and he said: "O Lord, have mercy on him, for I have already had mercy on him." Then Allah revealed to him: "Even if he calls upon Me until his strength gives out, I will not respond to him until he considers My right upon him."

Thus the servant's witnessing of the blessing and of the obligation leaves him no good deed that he sees, and he continues to belittle himself and to blame it; and he acknowledges that mercy is what he receives when he gives these two contemplations their due. And Allah is the One sought for help.

"He did not say: 'Indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise,' because the context is one of entreaty and of indirectly petitioning (for forgiveness), i.e., if You forgive them and have mercy on them, by enabling them to turn back from shirk to tawhid (divine unity), and from disobedience to obedience, as in the hadith: «O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know.»

In this there is the clearest indication that the Lord's names, may He be exalted, are derived from attributes and meanings subsisting in Him, and that every name fits what is mentioned alongside it and is linked with it, from His act and His command. And Allah is the Granter of success in what is correct."

In this there is the clearest indication that the Lord's names, may He be exalted, are derived from attributes and meanings subsisting in Him, and that every name fits what is mentioned alongside it and is linked with it, from His act and His command. And Allah is the Granter of success in what is correct."

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 14, verse 39:

As for the words of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Hearer of supplication﴾, the meaning of "hearing" here is special hearing, which is the hearing of response and acceptance, not general hearing, because He hears everything that is heard. Since this is so, "supplication" here encompasses both supplication of praise and supplication of request, and the Lord, blessed and exalted, hears it: He rewards the praise and responds to the request. So He hears this and that.

﴿Behind him is Hell﴾: the meaning is that he will meet Hell after his death, so it is after him, that is, after his departure from the world. Since it comes after his life, it is "behind him," because "warā'" (behind) is like "ba'd" (after). Just as "ba'd" cannot be "qabl" (before), "warā'" cannot be "amām" (in front). If you were to say "Hell is after the death of the disbeliever," there would be no sense of "before" in it in any way.

So "warā'" here refers to time, not place, so reflect on it, may God have mercy on you. It is behind the time of his life and after it, and it is in front of him and faces him.

So its being "behind" and "in front" is from two different perspectives. The confusion arose because temporal "after" applies to what lies ahead of you, as when you say "the day after tomorrow" (ba'd ghad), while spatial "behind" applies to what is left behind your back. So ﴿from behind him is Hell﴾ is "behind" in the sense of time, not place, and it applies only to the future that lies in front of you. Since the sense of "in front" is necessarily attached to it, whoever thought it was shared (between both senses) was mistaken; it is not shared. The same applies to His words ﴿and behind him is a harsh punishment﴾ and ﴿from behind him is Hell﴾.

As for His words ﴿and there was behind them a king﴾: if the reading "and there was in front of them a king" is authentic, it has a meaning that does not contradict the common reading, namely that the king was behind their backs, and their return was to him, so he was behind them in their going and in front of them in their returning. The two readings are thus according to two perspectives. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.
